newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends off as supplies viewed adequate.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends off as supplies viewed adequate.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower Tuesday on views of adequate supply while supply tightness in the New York Harbor pushed up gasoline prices.
"There is no mystery that there are plenty of barrels now in the Northeast," said a trader in Texas.
December heating oil ended 0.99 cent a gallon higher at 71.24 cents.
"People were having a hard time understanding why December heat should be gaining against January when there has been no problem with supply," said a trader.
Expectations of a minor build in distillate stocks in the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly oil inevntory data also pressured heating oil prices, traders said.
After the market's close Tuesday, the API reported that distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, grew 660,000 barrels for the week ended November 22.
December gasoline finished 1.02 cents up at 69.01 cents a gallon as a strong cash market in the New York Harbor was underpinned by lean supplies there.
January crude followed gasoline higher, ending up 13 cents at $23.62 a barrel.
However, chartists said danger may loom for January crude as a spot continuation chart reveals a head and shoulders pattern with the neckline at $22.85, the start of a gap made September 3.

"We have not recovered from that major reversal day on November 20, and if we don't close above the ($24.95) high that day, we will continue with the downtrend," said Jake Bernstein, president of MBH Commodity Advisors in Illinois.
The gap extends to $22.38, though crude has already closed the gap to $22.47.

In the headlines, several oil ministers at the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) meeting in Vienna have already called for a rollover of the group's 25.03 million barrel a day output quota before the meeting's official start Wednesday. Most traders have been expecting a rollover.
Bob MacMinn, chartist and president of MPAS Inc in Toronto, pegged support for January crude at $23.25, with a trading channel extending to $24.55.
"Whether we go below or above those levels will determine a longer term direction for crude," MacMinn said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
